content: 1. The effectiveness or concentration of atorvastatin may be reduced due to the impact of artemether/lumefantrine on hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the effectiveness or concentration of avanafil by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. For patients with erectile dysfunction (ED), monitor their response carefully due to the potential for reduced efficacy. 3. Both azithromycin and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Artemether/lumefantrine and bedaquiline both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring, including ECG monitoring, are recommended. 6. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Hydromorphone, a metabolite of hydrocodone, is primarily formed via CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation and may contribute to the overall analgesic effect of hydrocodone. 7. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of budesonide by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, budesonide may also reduce the effectiveness of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Co-administration of artemether/lumefantrine with bupivacaine implants may increase the toxicity of either drug. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Local anesthetics may elevate the risk of methemoglobinemia when combined with other drugs that also cause this condition. 9. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the effectiveness or concentration of buspirone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Butabarbital and butalbital may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of carbamazepine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Chloramphenicol may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of chlorpromazine by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of cilostazol by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of cinacalcet by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Both ciprofloxacin and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 17. Artemether/lumefantrine and citalopram both increase the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with caution when using other QT-prolonging drugs. 18. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of clopidogrel by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. CYP3A4 inducers may enhance the metabolism of clopidogrel to its active metabolite, potentially increasing antiplatelet effects. 19. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of clozapine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Cobicistat may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of codeine by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of colchicine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Conivaptan can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of conjugated estrogens (oral or vaginal) by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of cortisone by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, cortisone may also reduce the effectiveness of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Both crizotinib and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with caution when using other QT-prolonging drugs. 27. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of cyclosporine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, cyclosporine may increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Danazol may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of darifenacin by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, darifenacin may increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Darunavir can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Increased lumefantrine exposure may prolong the QT interval. 31. Dasatinib can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Both deutetrabenazine and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 33. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of dexamethasone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of dexfenfluramine by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 35. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of dextroamphetamine by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 36. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of dextromethorphan by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Herbal DHEA can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of diazepam by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of diltiazem by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, diltiazem may increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration may increase artemether/lumefantrine levels and toxicities, such as cardiac arrhythmias. 40. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of disopyramide by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Additive QTc prolongation effects may occur. Concomitant use with other QT-prolonging drugs, such as Class IA antiarrhythmics, should be avoided. 41. Both dolasetron and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of donepezil by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Dronedarone can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of eletriptan by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of encainide by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 46. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of erlotinib by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of estradiol by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 48. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of synthetic conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 50. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 52. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of exemestane by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. For patients receiving exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose of exemestane is 50 mg daily after a meal. 54. Co-administration of artemether/lumefantrine with ezogabine may increase the toxicity of either drug due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to increase the QT interval. 55. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of fesoterodine by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, it may reduce the effectiveness of fesoterodine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 57. Both flecainide and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 58. Fluconazole can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of fludrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, fludrocortisone may also reduce the effectiveness of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 60. Both fluoxetine and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of fluphenazine by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 62. Fosamprenavir can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 63. Fosaprepitant can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 64. Both foscarnet and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 65. Both artemether/lumefantrine and fostemsavir can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 66. Both artemether/lumefantrine and gemtuzumab can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 67. Both gepirone and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 68. Grapefruit can increase the concentration or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 69. Griseofulvin may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 70. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of guanfacine by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 71. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of hydrocodone by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Hydromorphone, a metabolite of hydrocodone, is primarily formed via CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation and may contribute to the overall analgesic effect of hydrocodone. 72. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of hydrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, hydrocortisone may also reduce the effectiveness of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 73. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the concentration or effect of hydromorphone by influencing CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 74. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by altering CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 75. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Both iloperidone and artemether/lumefantrine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 76. Co-administration of artemether/lumefantrine with inhaled indacaterol may increase the risk of QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 77. Artemether/lumefantrine may reduce the effectiveness or concentration of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
